_comment: Recommended libraries & tools directory (Ctrl+B). Loaded by src/libraries.js and merged with an optional config/libraries.local.json (gitignored) - a local category with the same title REPLACES the base one. Category titles are localized { pl, en }; item descriptions are plain strings, i.e. language-neutral: they are technical blurbs, not UI chrome. Each category also names an `icon` - a slug, never a glyph and never markup - which src/renderer/modules/libicons.js draws as an SVG; an unknown or malformed name falls back to the neutral `default` tile. Item ids are DERIVED from the name by the loader - do not write them here. `url` must be http(s). The renderer never hands an address back to the main process; it names an id and main resolves the URL from this file.

items.name: daisyUI
items.description: Tailwind plugin that turns utility soup into semantic class names (btn, card, modal). Pure CSS with no JS runtime, 68 components, and 68 built-in themes that swap through a data attribute.

items.name: Kokonut UI
items.description: 100+ React components on Tailwind, Motion and shadcn/ui, taken either by the shadcn CLI or pasted in whole. The source ships with the component, so an agent edits it instead of fighting a package API. The Pro tier is separate and paid.

items.name: OriginKit
items.description: Free library of animated components for modern websites. Documentation is thin - the gallery is the reference, so budget time to read the source of anything you take.

items.name: Motion
items.description: Animation for React, Vue and plain JS on a hybrid engine: hardware-accelerated browser APIs where they exist, JS where they do not. Successor to Framer Motion, MIT, and small enough that scroll-linked work no longer needs GSAP.

items.name: Particles (Casberry)
items.description: Browser studio for particle swarms on Three.js/WebGL - 20k+ units, behaviour written as a JS function you generate with an LLM and paste in. Exports vanilla JS, React or Three.js, plus PLY/GLB/OBJ. A workbench, not a drop-in background component.

items.name: Bklit UI
items.description: React chart components: 17+ types from area and bar through sankey, sunburst and candlestick, with the axes, legends and brushes around them. Ships a visual builder (Studio) and prebuilt blocks; open source, in the Vercel OSS program.

items.name: Manus
items.description: Hosted agent that runs multi-step work on its own - slides, sites, images, music, driving a browser. Closed and cloud-side on paid tiers: you hand it a goal, not a tool loop you control.

items.name: cloudflare/computer
items.description: A virtual filesystem living inside a Durable Object, SQLite as the source of truth, projected into a container, a bash isolate or a JS isolate so a sandbox keeps its working state between calls. Cloudflare says plainly it is not production-ready - experiments only.

items.name: usestrix/strix
items.description: Agents that pentest a running app from a Docker sandbox and prove each finding with a working PoC - the part that separates it from a scanner emitting maybes. Can open remediation PRs. Needs an LLM key, and authorised targets only.

items.name: mvanhorn/last30days-skill
items.description: Pulls the last 30 days from Reddit, HN, Polymarket, GitHub and arXiv with no keys at all; X, YouTube and the rest each need their own auth. Ranks by real engagement and writes Markdown, HTML or JSON. Already installed here - see the /last30days command.

items.name: cathrynlavery/diagram-design
items.description: Agent skill that emits 39 diagram types as self-contained HTML+SVG - no build step, no JS runtime - and can redraw an existing draw.io, Mermaid or Excalidraw source. Exports SVG and PNG. Also installed here.

items.name: tt-a1i/archify
items.description: You describe a system in chat, the agent emits typed JSON, and Archify compiles that deterministically into one interactive HTML file. Five diagram kinds; pointing it at a repo is optional, and only there to pin claims to commits.

items.name: unclecode/crawl4ai
items.description: Crawler whose output target is a context window, not a browser: clean Markdown plus CSS/XPath/LLM extraction, page chrome already stripped. Deep crawling, stealth mode and a Docker server. Apache-2.0.

items.name: Panniantong/Agent-Reach
items.description: Gives an agent one way in to 16+ platforms - X, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, XiaoHongShu - by routing each to whichever backend still works: official API, CLI tool, browser or scrape, with health checks and fallbacks. The routing table is the product.

items.name: browser-use/browser-use
items.description: Lets an agent work a real web UI from the DOM and from screenshots, which is what gets it through flows a selector-only script would lose. Python 3.11+, any major LLM or their own tuned model, a local browser or their cloud.

items.name: AKCodez/seo-god
items.description: Turns Claude Code into a standing SEO operator: audits the site, fixes what it can in your repo, reads Search Console, tracks AI-answer visibility, then installs itself as a daily job. Needs Docker and a publicly reachable site. It edits files but never commits them.

items.name: JCodesMore/ai-website-cloner-template
items.description: Point an agent at a URL and it rebuilds the site as Next.js 16, React 19, shadcn/ui and Tailwind v4, extracting design tokens, assets and per-component specs on the way. MIT, and the README is blunt about not using it to impersonate anyone.

items.name: diegosouzapw/OmniRoute
items.description: Local gateway with an OpenAI-compatible /v1 in front of 350+ providers, cascading subscription to key to cheap to free as each one fails. 19 routing strategies and a prompt-compression stage; also speaks MCP.

items.name: jamiepine/voicebox
items.description: Local voice studio: seven TTS engines, zero-shot cloning from one sample, Whisper dictation on a global hotkey, and an MCP server so an agent can speak in a chosen voice. Nothing leaves the machine. Rust and React, MIT.

items.name: guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover
items.description: Strips invisible-Unicode carriers and C2PA/EXIF/XMP provenance from text and media you own, and rewrites text to attack sampling watermarks. Honest about the trade: the rewrite flattens the prose, and no tool can certify a mark is actually gone.

items.name: pranshuparmar/witr
items.description: Answers "why is this running?" - walks PID ancestry, the supervisor above a process (systemd, launchd, Services, rc.d) and the ports and files below it, then prints the causal chain. Linux, macOS, Windows and FreeBSD; plain text, JSON or a TUI.

items.name: vitali87/code-graph-rag
items.description: Tree-sitter parse of 13+ languages into a Memgraph or Neo4j knowledge graph, queried by turning a question into Cypher. Also does AST-based edits and dead-code detection. Same idea as the codebase-memory MCP already wired into this setup.

items.name: public-apis/public-apis
items.description: The long-running index of free public APIs by category, each row carrying its auth type and whether it supports HTTPS and CORS - which is the part worth the visit. A starting point: entries go stale and auth requirements drift.

items.name: livekit/agents
items.description: Voice agents as WebRTC participants: the STT-LLM-TTS loop plus a transformer that decides when you have actually finished talking, which is what makes interruption bearable. Multi-agent handoff and telephony included. Python, Apache-2.0.

items.name: langflow-ai/langflow
items.description: Node-graph editor for agent workflows, with Python behind every node and export either as an API or as an MCP server. MIT, Python 3.10-3.14, desktop build available. The visual layer earns its keep when handing a flow to someone else.

items.name: langgenius/dify
items.description: Self-hostable platform covering workflows, RAG, agents and prompt iteration - heavier than a library, lighter than building the ops layer yourself. The licence is Apache-2.0 with extra conditions, so read it before shipping on top.

items.name: xiamuceer-j/MuMuAINovel
items.description: Long-form fiction drafting that keeps what a novel needs - characters, worldbuilding, relationship graph, planted foreshadowing - in Postgres rather than the context window. FastAPI and React, deployed with Docker.

items.name: GVCLab/PersonaLive
items.description: Streaming diffusion that animates a still portrait from a driving video, continuously and without a fixed length. 12GB of VRAM is the floor, which is the number that decides whether it runs on your machine. Released for academic research only.

items.name: aiming-lab/AutoResearchClaw
items.description: A 23-stage pipeline from topic to conference-formatted LaTeX: literature search across OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and arXiv, sandboxed self-healing experiments, multi-agent review, verified BibTeX. Three human approval gates - leave them in.

items.name: Zackriya-Solutions/meetily
items.description: Meeting notes with nothing leaving the machine: Rust and Tauri app, local Whisper or Parakeet transcription, summaries through Ollama or a cloud key if you want one. Speaker diarization is not in the community build yet.

items.name: coollabsio/coolify
items.description: Self-hosted deploy layer for apps, databases and 300+ one-click services on anything you can SSH into, down to a Raspberry Pi. Git-push deploys and PR previews - the usual answer to a Vercel bill that stopped being small.

items.name: CoreBunch/Instatic
items.description: Visual CMS on Bun where pages, posts and any collection you invent share one table, and publishing bakes plain semantic HTML to disk - no framework runtime left in the page, and about a kilobyte of it only where something is genuinely dynamic.

items.name: Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF
items.description: 50+ PDF tools - merge, split, convert, OCR, redact, sign - as a desktop app, a browser build or a server you host, so documents stop going through a random web converter. Open-core: some enterprise pieces are not free.

items.name: brag
items.description: Agent skill that turns the repo itself into a shareable launch video: it picks the angle, then renders an MP4 with music and share copy into brag-output/. /brag, --voice for narration, --tone to steer it. Needs Node 22, FFmpeg and the Hyperframes CLI.

items.name: autoclip
items.description: A self-hosted service rather than a CLI: pulls a video from YouTube or Bilibili, has an LLM outline it, scores the segments, titles the winners and assembles themed collections. FastAPI, Celery and Redis behind a React UI.

items.name: vhs
items.description: Terminal GIF and video recorder written in Go, driven by declarative .tape scripts - a demo clip becomes a file you re-run, not a take you re-record. Outputs GIF, MP4, WebM or frames; needs ttyd and ffmpeg on PATH.

items.name: claude-video
items.description: A /watch skill that lets Claude actually see a video: yt-dlp for the source, ffmpeg for frames, captions or Whisper for a timestamped transcript, then answers grounded in both. It reads video - it does not generate any.

items.name: video-use
items.description: An editing agent despite the name: point it at a folder of raw takes and it transcribes with ElevenLabs Scribe, cuts filler and silence from the TEXT, grades, subtitles and renders edit/final.mp4. Nothing to do with driving a browser.

items.name: OpenMontage
items.description: Agentic pipeline from one sentence to a finished MP4 - research, script, scene plan, asset generation, edit, compose - across 60+ providers, with an approval gate and a spend cap at each stage. Composes through Remotion or HyperFrames. AGPLv3.

items.name: Remotion
items.description: Videos written as React components and rendered frame by frame, locally, on Lambda or in the browser - so a clip is code you can diff, parametrize and rebuild. Not plain open source: past a certain company size it needs a paid licence.

items.name: FFmpeg
items.description: The command-line audio/video toolkit this app's own highlight extractor shells out to for trimming clips - and what half the entries above already quietly depend on. Not bundled; grab a static build for your OS from this page and make sure it lands on PATH.
